overall_assessment: All 19 offerings yielded sections, the English headings mapped consistently, and the learning outcomes were intact. The 12 empty flags identified placeholder rows, while the long flag prompted a closer look at FRI310, where the extractor missed an entry requirement under the admission heading. The six random controls also exposed unflagged placeholders, exam gates filed under other sections, and assessment logistics.

findings.description: Eleven prerequisite rows contain only ‘No subjects’ with optional punctuation, and the flagged THP301 reading-list row contains only ‘Core reading.’ Two longer prerequisite negations passed the pre-pass, as did the bare labels ‘Core reading for.’ and ‘Reading list for’. Two 2023 controls also emit a stock redirect to the annual Study Handbook archive as a reading list. The blank Core literature headings elsewhere correctly yield no row.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The placeholder patterns in R/extract_sections.R miss these English NIH variants, including the translation of the stock Study Handbook redirect already covered in Norwegian.
findings.suggested_fix: Add whole-row patterns for the observed prerequisite negations, bare reading-list labels and stock archive redirect. Scope the patterns to their respective sections and preserve rows with actual requirements, readings or a course-specific reading-list link.

findings.evidence: Individual course applicants must have completed 60 ECTS credits in outdoor studies to qualify for admission.
findings.description: FRI310's long prerequisite row describes physical abilities needed to complete the course and refers to the programme schedule. It omits the substantive prior-study requirement of 60 ECTS in outdoor studies for individual applicants. The length flag points to the affected row but does not detect the omitted requirement.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/section_heading_map.R maps ‘Admission to the course’ to .drop, so the entire block is dropped despite the explicit prior-study requirement.
findings.suggested_fix: For NIH's English pages, route ‘Admission to the course’ through .admission and make .admission_prerequisites() retain English sentences specifying completed ECTS in a named subject. Preserve the restriction to individual applicants and filter application and enrolment boilerplate.

findings.evidence: Group assignment in the format of oral presentation during course. Approved/not approved.
findings.description: MAS449 files the approval-only oral presentation in assessment and its exam-eligibility rule in teaching methods, leaving coursework requirements absent. MA531 repeats the assignment gate in teaching methods despite a separate coursework row. Three THP111 offerings likewise leave a mandatory module-quiz statement in teaching methods even though the coursework section identifies the quiz as part of the work to approve before final assessment.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The mapped headings supply the initial boundaries, but the coursework gate handling in R/extract_sections.R misses these English approval and exam-eligibility formulations.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the gate rules to recognise ‘forfeits the right to take the final examination’, approval-only group presentations corroborated by an exam-gate sentence, and mandatory module quizzes corroborated by a pre-exam approval rule. Move those statements into coursework_requirements, create the row where absent, and avoid repeating requirements already stated there.

findings.evidence: English is the primary language of the course, however those students who wish can complete the assignments and the exam in Norwegian.
findings.description: The Introduction block is extracted wholesale as course content. In MA531 this leaves the permitted exam language out of assessment. In MAS449 the opening paragraph mixes intensive teaching and exam arrangements into course content. Four LKI152 offerings likewise carry their documentary-style teaching format under course content.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The ‘Introduction’ mapping in R/section_heading_map.R applies to the full block and R/extract_sections.R has no NIH sentence rules for these mixed introductions.
findings.suggested_fix: Use NIH-specific sentence or clause rules for the observed introductions. Route explicit exam-language options to assessment and identifiable descriptions of delivery to teaching_methods. Keep the subject-matter text and avoid repeating assessment components already described under Assessment/exam.

findings.evidence: The project assignment must be submitted in Wiseflow during a designated submission period at the end of the semester.
findings.description: Assessment rows retain submission platforms, task-release timing and submission windows alongside graded exam design. SPM123 and SPM104 describe the semester submission window, while the MA453 control includes a WISEflow delivery clause in the same sentence as plagiarism screening. Actual exam duration and plagiarism or AI rules belong in assessment.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The logistics cleanup in R/extract_sections.R lacks NIH English patterns for these sentences and clauses.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip the observed English task-release and submission-window sentences and add clause-level rules for WISEflow delivery. When a sentence combines delivery with plagiarism screening, preserve the screening clause and retain genuine timed exam durations.
